head: working-tree
subject: MQTT topic-filter validation checks wildcard positions directly
change: validTopicFilterLevels previously split the filter on every slash and ran separate '#' and '+' searches per level. It now uses indexOfAnyPos to find each wildcard and checks only that position: the wildcard must occupy a complete level, and '#' must also be the final byte. Filters without wildcards need one SIMD search and no level walk, while wildcard filters avoid the per-level split and repeated scalar searches. The accepted grammar is unchanged. The shared MQTT UTF-8 validator also checks sixteen-byte ASCII chunks with vector comparisons before falling back to the scalar prefix scan, so ordinary ASCII topic names and filters avoid a byte-at-a-time loop. Retained wildcard lookups now build one mqtt.FilterMatcher per filter: the filter's level boundaries are computed once, and each stored topic is matched against those boundaries instead of re-splitting the filter for every entry. Filters deeper than the inline 32-level bound fall back to topicMatchesFilter. FilterMatcher also recognizes filters whose only wildcard is a final '#': the preceding levels must be literal, so matching reduces to one prefix comparison instead of walking every filter and topic level. '#' alone matches every non-'$'-reserved topic, and 'prefix/#' accepts the prefix itself or any topic below it. The retained Store now keeps a parallel LevelIndex array with the end offset of up to four levels per stored topic, computed once on insert. Wildcard matching passes those ends to FilterMatcher.matchesEntry, so a repeated scan no longer splits every topic on '/' for every filter. The index lives outside Entry so ordinary entry copies and exact lookups keep their original size; topics deeper than four levels fall back to the split matcher.

mqtt_interop.note: full Mosquitto-derived broker configuration matrix, including retained state, shared subscriptions, ACL reloads and persistence. It passed again after the parallel topic level-index change.

notes: The retained store exact-lookup path calls validateTopicFilter, effectiveFilter and hasWildcards before its hash-map lookup. Removing the per-level split cuts the validation portion enough to nearly halve the exact lookup time. The wildcard full-scan case improves because validation no longer splits every level before matching. Empty filters are still rejected before any scan, and the wildcard-position checks preserve the exact grammar: '+' must be a complete level, and '#' must be a complete final level. The full broker-config matrix passes in isolation; the one earlier timeout occurred while the complete library test was running concurrently and is attributed to host-load contention rather than the filter change. The vector UTF-8 prefix check preserves the scalar error semantics for NUL, high bytes and the strict-control policy; a chunk with any non-ASCII byte falls back to the scalar scan from that chunk. The retained matcher preserves splitScalar semantics for empty levels and trailing slashes, the MQTT '$' leading-wildcard reservation, and '#' termination. Exact retained lookups stay on the hash index and are unaffected. The trailing-'#' fast path preserves the '$' leading-wildcard reservation, the zero-level '#' match on the prefix itself, and filters with '+' before '#' still use the level walk. The LevelIndex array is parallel to the tombstone-preserving entry table; remove leaves the slot for reuse and insert overwrites it. Exact retained lookups still use the hash index and do not touch the level array.

utf8_vector_benchmark.note: The host was loaded during this batch; only the interleaved ratio is claimed.

hash_filter_benchmark.note: The benchmark now includes a devices/# scenario. A first batch under host load showed the same hash direction with a larger ratio; the reported values are the quieter repeat batch.

level_index_benchmark.note: A first batch measured exact 0.952x, wildcard 1.440x and hash 0.989x; the reported quieter repeat batch keeps the same wildcard direction.
